axis_reasons.H: Selected prose, captions and displayed card facts agree with canonical observations. Date-only status, reported seats and unknown price scope are preserved. No confirmed itinerary, cross-program value ordering, invented balances or availability is asserted.
axis_reasons.U: Pass at the no-complete threshold: names real endpoint research leads and explicitly directs the traveler to verify complete itineraries and applicable charges with each program, then current availability/prices on official booking sites. This does not establish strong comparative usefulness.
axis_reasons.M2: Three consecutive captions largely repeat card prices and the identical date-only/unknown-scope caveat. United and Aeroplan are introduced only as another research lead; the answer does not explain why each adds a useful choice. Common limitations are repeated per card and again in the closing paragraph. The resulting sequence lacks connected individual reasoning despite a correct opening and closing.
axis_reasons.C: No meaningful supported comparison is developed. Cross-program points are correctly declared incomparable, but the full month source has same-program date and cabin contrasts that can guide a research check without claiming itinerary or economic superiority. Selecting three January 1 economy quotes and restating their fields does not explain a choice.
axis_reasons.K: No Ranking style is invented: source alternatives, assessments, comparison_pool_ids and style indexes are empty, as are selected journey IDs and resolved ranking_assessments.
axis_reasons.P: Three actual lead_card blocks exactly resolve to source components and HTML article cards; one cash_sentence is bound to the quoted USD 640 observation. All 383 canonical component identities remain in evidence; all 378 award references/leads and five cash references are retained. Pass is limited to the supplied artifact/data boundary; no interactive explorer UI was supplied or tested.
